_comment: THE WHOLE-SPINE A/B REGISTRY. One row: `sim_closure`, whose A/B arm is the SHIP configuration
(`[config] mode=brokered`, i.e. tools/uiscripts/ini/ship_config.ini overriding nothing) and whose
control arm is `[config] mode=original` -- the game running its own bodies end to end. That pair is
IT HELD 22 ROWS UNTIL FORK F2E. The other 21 were PER-MODULE bisect rows: each named one
`[promote]` key, and migration_ab flipped that key to 0 to build a control arm differing from ship
in exactly one module. F2E deleted the `[promote]` section -- which bodies run is `[config] mode`
and nothing else, and a surviving section now refuses the run by name -- so a per-module control
arm can no longer be expressed. The rows went with their 21 ini fragments rather than being left as
a registry of configurations the DLL would reject.
FIELDS (unchanged): key / function / ini / poke_region / live_served / ship_default / vehicle, plus
`control` and `installed_key` for the whole-closure row -- `sim_closure` names the whole ship
configuration, so its fragment cannot carry `sim_closure=1` and its liveness is read off the key it

modules.live_served: \[promote\] sim_step body served call #(\d+) from game code
modules.why: SIM1-P clause 3: the WHOLE-CLOSURE A/B. Not one key -- the ship configuration against the entire DLL rolled back, which is the oracle that replaces the per-body shadow sites clause 2's rebind dissolves. Its liveness signal is sim_step's own served counter, because every one of the 530 rows is reached through that root or through a body it calls. INSTALLED_KEY: sim_step -- there is no `[promote] sim_closure:` line (this key names the ship config, not a seam), so without the override this module reported installed=False forever and its verdict was structurally NOT_LIVE.
